title: Institutional FX Dashboard & Intelligence Report — July 14, 2026

regime.classification: Event-Driven, dual-track — a genuine "good news on inflation, bad news on geopolitics" session, with US June CPI cooling sharply even as the Iran/Strait of Hormuz crisis escalated to its most severe point yet.
regime.justification: US equities rose (S&P 500 +0.38% to 7,543.59, Nasdaq +0.9% to 26,107.01 on semiconductor strength, Dow roughly flat +0.02% to 52,508.27) and the US 10Y yield fell to 4.583% on a much cooler-than-expected June CPI print — yet VIX rose 14.2% to 17.16 anyway, an unusual divergence that reflects the Iran/Hormuz war-risk premium building underneath a rates-driven equity rally rather than genuine calm. Oil extended its rally sharply further (Brent +3.7% to +4.5% depending on source, into the mid-$80s), the highest level of this entire crisis.
regime.executiveSummary: Today was dominated by two simultaneous, partly offsetting stories. First, US June CPI surprised sharply to the downside: headline CPI fell 0.4% m/m (vs. -0.2% expected), pulling the annual rate to 3.5% (vs. 3.8% expected, down from May's 4.2%); core CPI was flat m/m (vs. +0.2% expected) at 2.6% y/y (vs. 2.9% expected) — a genuine, broad-based cooling led by a 5.7% m/m energy drop (the largest since April 2020) and flat services-ex-energy costs. Treasury yields fell and the dollar retreated broadly on the print. However, new Fed (US Federal Reserve) Chair Kevin Warsh's first congressional testimony (House Financial Services Committee) pushed back hard against a dovish read, stating the Committee has "no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation" and that today's data is not "mission accomplished" — keeping the September hike debate alive rather than closing it. Separately, Q2 bank earnings from JPMorgan (a large beat, EPS $6.14 vs. $5.85 expected) and Wells Fargo (EPS $2.00 vs. $1.72 expected) added a positive equity-market undertone. Second, and overshadowing the CPI relief by session's end, the Iran/Strait of Hormuz crisis escalated further: the US reimposed a full naval blockade of Iranian ports (effective 20:00 GMT) alongside fresh strikes near Sirik and Bandar Abbas, while Iran retaliated with strikes on shipping in Omani waters (reportedly killing a crew member) and attacks on Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan — Kuwait's navy intercepted a ballistic missile, five cruise missiles, and 33 drones in a single wave. Trump separately scrapped his proposed 20% Hormuz transit toll, replacing it with bilateral trade deals with Gulf allies — a partial economic-track de-escalation gesture even as the military conflict intensified. USD/JPY eased modestly to ~162.20 on the broad-dollar pullback, still without any distinct safe-haven bid despite the crisis's worst day yet.

**Educational Breakdown — Long NZD/USD (closed, full win):**

*What we expected, and why:* The thesis, published 4 Jul, was short-covering plus a hawkish RBNZ repricing building into the 8 Jul decision. At publication it scored 65/100 overall, with Positioning as the strongest relative signal (15/20 — NZD shorts had already unwound to a 6-month low) and Macro contributing the most raw points (24/35 — "RBNZ pivot narrative building but decision still ahead"). Technicals were deliberately weak (14/25 — "lagging peers on spot, no fresh breakout confirmed"), and the report named an explicit, dated confirmation trigger: watch the 8 Jul RBNZ statement for hawkish language before adding.

*What actually happened:* The RBNZ delivered exactly that trigger — a 25bp hike on 8 Jul, its first in three years. That single dated event became a genuinely durable, eight-session catalyst: NZD/USD ground from the ~0.5655 entry midpoint through the first target (0.5750, hit ~13 Jul) and on to the second (0.5820, hit intraday 14 Jul).

*Match or divergence — and why:* This matched. The most predictive element wasn't the raw macro score (a middling 24/35) — it was the combination of already-unwound positioning (nowhere left for shorts to cover) plus a specific, dated event the report told readers to watch for. When a thesis names an exact confirmation trigger rather than a vague "bullish backdrop," and positioning has already cleared out the crowded side of the trade, the setup tends to have real follow-through once the trigger fires. The weak Technicals score at publication (14/25) wasn't a warning sign here — it was simply too early; technical confirmation followed the fundamental catalyst rather than leading it, worth flagging for anyone who defaults to reading price action first.

**Running Hit Rate: 1 played out (fully resolved — both targets hit) / 0 invalidated / 3 still pending, out of 4 total ideas issued since July 4, 2026 (first-run date of the merged structure).** Short AUD/NZD, now just ~13 pips from its own first target, is the item to watch most closely for tomorrow's review — a genuine second win could land within the next session or two.

**Known data gap flagged:** No dated, sourced CFTC positioning update specific to this week could be confirmed via live search this session (see Section 17) — all positioning characterizations above are carried forward from the most recently confirmed reads.

sections.title: Layer-by-Layer Synthesis
sections.raw:
**NZD/USD**
- *Data Layer:* Intraday high 0.5822 today, clearing the second published target (0.5820); later quotes show 0.5789-0.5808. RBNZ policy rate 2.50%.
- *Macro Layer:* The RBNZ's (New Zealand) 8 Jul hike has now driven the pair to both published targets over eight sessions — a genuinely durable catalyst, one of the cleanest confirmed theses in this report's short history.
- *Market Structure Layer:* Both technical objectives (0.5750, 0.5820) have now been reached — this idea has done everything a leveled thesis is meant to do.
- *Positioning Layer:* No fresh CFTC read confirmed this session; the "unsettled NZD positioning" characterization from early July is now entirely stale given eight sessions of one-directional, target-confirming follow-through.
- *Sentiment Layer:* Today's broad-dollar weakness (cool CPI) added a same-direction tailwind on top of the RBNZ catalyst, helping push the pair through its final target.
- *Decision Layer:* This idea should be formally closed out at the next run as a full, double-target win — the clearest complete success this report series has produced. No further tracking needed beyond noting the outcome in the historical hit-rate tally.

**Short AUD/NZD**
- *Data Layer:* Intraday low 1.19629 today, ~13 pips above the first published target (1.1950) — down sharply from several sessions stalled near 1.2117.
- *Macro Layer:* The underlying case (confirmed RBNZ hike, soft China CPI) is reinforced today by NZD's own broad strength on the target-2 hit — two forces now pulling in the same direction for this cross.
- *Market Structure Layer:* A decisive break below the prior 2 Jul low (1.2134) that this report has flagged for several sessions — the clearest technical progress this idea has shown.
- *Positioning Layer:* No fresh CFTC read confirmed this session; same staleness caveat as other ideas.
- *Sentiment Layer:* Today's genuinely more mixed risk backdrop (equities up, VIX also up on Hormuz risk) is not a clean read either way for this idea specifically.
- *Decision Layer:* With price now essentially at the first target, the next run should watch closely for either a confirmed touch/close through 1.1950 (partial win, watch for 1.1850) or a bounce back into the prior range.

sections.title: Correlation Check
sections.raw:
EUR/USD and GBP/USD both firmed today, moving in the same direction — their normal positive correlation remains intact, both reflecting the same broad-dollar-weakness theme from the cool June CPI print. NZD/USD's much larger move (clearing its second target) stands out as this report's clearest idiosyncratic driver, now more a story of NZD's own multi-week strength than a dollar-weakness story alone — AUD/NZD's sharp breakdown today is best read as an extension of that same NZD-specific strength rather than a fresh AUD-specific catalyst.

**Read: Clean** — with the NZD/RBNZ story remaining the one well-explained idiosyncratic exception to an otherwise broad-dollar-driven day, now joined by AUD/NZD's break lower as a direct extension of that same exception rather than a second, separate one.

sections.title: Contrarian Check & Risks
sections.raw:
**Primary thesis risk:** The Iran/Hormuz situation remains capable of moving sharply in either direction on short notice — Trump's same-day reversal on the transit toll shows genuine two-way headline risk even amid the crisis's worst escalation yet. Separately, tomorrow brings a genuine double catalyst (BoC decision, Chair Warsh's second day of congressional testimony before the Senate) that could move both USD/CAD and the broader dollar sharply.

**Overall-view invalidation factor:** A confirmed, sustained de-escalation in Iran/Hormuz — not just a single reversed policy announcement — combined with a dovish-leaning tone from Warsh's Senate testimony tomorrow would be the cleanest scenario to accelerate the dollar's pullback and open further room for the Short USD/JPY thesis.

- **Bull case (for this report's ideas):** AUD/NZD closes through its first target (1.1950) as NZD strength persists; USD/JPY extends its modest pullback on continued dollar softness. *Invalidated by:* a confirmed, sustained break of 163.50 in USD/JPY or 1.2250 in AUD/NZD.
- **Base case:** AUD/NZD consolidates just above its first target without a confirmed close through it; USD/JPY holds broadly within its recent range pending tomorrow's BoC decision and Warsh testimony. *Invalidated by:* a decisive break in either pair's key level.
- **Bear case (for this report's ideas):** A hawkish surprise from Warsh's Senate testimony or a fresh Iran/Hormuz escalation reverses today's dollar weakness, USD/JPY grinds back toward its highs, and AUD/NZD bounces back above 1.2100. *Invalidated by:* continued dollar softness and a confirmed AUD/NZD close through 1.1950.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first congressional testimony before the House Financial Services Committee (already delivered — see Sections 1/3). **Ongoing:** the Iran/Strait of Hormuz crisis escalated to its most severe point yet today (reimposed naval blockade, fresh strikes, multi-country Iranian retaliation).

sections.title: No-Trade Zone Flag
sections.raw: **Yes — elevated.** Today combined a genuine positive macro surprise (cool CPI) with the worst single-day escalation of the Iran/Hormuz crisis so far, plus a hawkish-leaning central-bank testimony actively resisting the market's dovish read of that data — a lot of cross-currents resolving in different directions at once. Tomorrow adds a live BoC decision and Warsh's second testimony day. Despite the Clean correlation read and real technical progress in this report's two open ideas, the concentration of live, two-way risk argues for continued close monitoring over adding fresh single-pair exposure.

sections.title: Key Theme Driving Everything Right Now
sections.raw:
1. **US June CPI cooled sharply (headline 3.5% y/y, core 2.6% y/y, both well below consensus), but Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first congressional testimony pushed back hard against a dovish market read**, keeping the September-hike debate genuinely open rather than resolved — a real tension between the data and the Fed's own messaging.
2. **The Iran/Strait of Hormuz crisis escalated to its most severe point yet — a reimposed naval blockade, fresh US strikes, and Iranian retaliation across four countries (Oman, Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan) — even as Trump reversed his own transit-toll proposal the same day**, underscoring how fast this situation can still turn in either direction.
3. **NZD/USD has now cleared both published targets, the tracker's first fully complete win, while Short AUD/NZD's sharp breakdown today (intraday low just 13 pips from target) makes it the idea most likely to deliver a second win within the next session or two.**

sections.title: Decision Dashboard Snapshot
sections.raw:
**Overall Market Confidence: 55/100** (∆ vs last report: +5). The improvement reflects genuine positive technical progress in this report's two open ideas (AUD/NZD nearing target, USD/JPY's first favorable session in a while) and NZD/USD's full resolution as a win, outweighing the further escalation in Iran/Hormuz systemic risk and the added uncertainty from tomorrow's BoC decision and Warsh's second testimony day.

**Portfolio Tilt Note:** Long-NZD/USD idea now fully resolved (both targets hit) — should be formally closed out at the next run. Short-AUD/NZD tilt strengthened materially given today's decisive technical breakdown, now the highest-confidence idea this report series has produced. Short-JPY-carry-fade tilt modestly improved for the first time in several sessions, though still the weaker of the two open ideas. The Iran/Hormuz oil shock remains flagged as a live, unhedged macro risk factor across the book generally. Informational context only — explicitly not a personalized allocation recommendation.

sections.title: Historical Parallel Watch
sections.raw: No strong historical parallel today. The Iran/Strait of Hormuz escalation remains fundamentally a geopolitical/commodity shock with FX and rates as second-order effects, not a clean match for any of the four FX-positioning-specific archetypes. Today's Fed dynamic — cooling data met with a chair actively resisting a dovish market read — has a loose echo of central banks "talking tough" against market expectations in past cycles, but this is a common enough central-bank behavior that it doesn't rise to a genuine, specific historical parallel worth naming.
